Sardine Stone
SAR-dine STONE
noun
From the Greek sardinos, said to be named from Sardis in Lydia, where the stone was found or traded; a deep blood-red carnelian. This entry treats the Revelation 4 throne-vision word; for the breastplate stone see sardius.

Biblical Definition

The sardine stone is the deep blood-red carnelian, and in the Authorized Version the phrase belongs to one place above all others — the throne room of heaven. John is called up through the open door and sees no form and no face, only light and colour: “And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne” (Rev 4:2). “And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald” (Rev 4:3). Mark what John does not describe. There is no attempt at a face, no human likeness, no portrait of God — only the flash of two stones and the arc of a third. The jasper is clear and white as crystal (Rev 21:11), the light of holiness and untouchable purity; the sardine is red as blood, the fire of justice and the price of redemption. Holiness and judgment together, and encircling both a rainbow, the sign sworn to Noah that the flood shall not return — mercy bending round the throne of the Judge. The same stone appears as sardius in the sixth foundation of the New Jerusalem’s wall (Rev 21:20). Before this throne the elders cast their crowns and say, “Thou art worthy, O Lord” (Rev 4:11).

Webster 1828 Definition

A deep blood-red carnelian; in Rev 4:3 the colour under which the One seated on heaven’s throne appeared to John.

SARDINE STONE, a precious stone of a deep blood-red colour; the carnelian or sard.

Greek sardinos, said to be named from Sardis in Lydia.

In Rev 4:3 it describes the appearance of Him that sat upon the throne.

It is paired with the crystal-clear jasper, and encircled by an emerald rainbow.

The same stone stands as sardius in the sixth foundation of the city wall (Rev 21:20).

Key Scripture

Rev 4:2 — "And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne."

Rev 4:3 — "And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald."

Rev 21:20 — "The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, a topaz; the tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst."

Rev 4:11 — "Thou art worthy, O Lord, to receive glory and honour and power: for thou hast created all things, and for thy pleasure they are and were created."

Modern Corruption

The throne vision is mined for gemstone symbolism and crystal lore, when its point is that John saw colour and light and no likeness at all — and that the throne is occupied.

expand to see more

Two live misuses attach to this stone. The first is the trade in gemstone mysticism — birthstones, chakras, crystals charged with energies — which finds in Rev 4:3 and Rev 21:20 a biblical veneer for a thoroughly pagan practice. Scripture never assigns power to a stone. The jasper and the sardine are John’s only available vocabulary for a glory that has no earthly likeness; the stones are borrowed for their light, not credited with virtue. The second and subtler misuse is a devotional one: the modern appetite for a God who can be pictured, felt, and made familiar. John, given the nearest look at heaven any man in Scripture received, reports no face. He gives colour, fire, sound, and a rainbow, and nothing that a painter could set on canvas — which is precisely the second commandment holding at the highest altitude. The vision that most tempts us to imagine is the vision that most firmly refuses the image.

Read the colours as the text sets them. Jasper: clear, crystalline, white — the unapproachable holiness of God, the light no man can approach unto. Sardine: blood-red — His justice, and the blood by which that justice was satisfied, so that the Lamb standing in the midst of the throne looks as it had been slain. Rainbow, in sight like unto an emerald: the covenant sign given after the flood, the sworn mercy of God, drawn as a complete circle round the whole throne. Holiness, judgment, and covenant mercy, and none of the three at the expense of the others. And the first thing the vision establishes is not a colour but a fact: a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. The seat is not empty and never has been. Everything that follows in the book — seals, trumpets, vials, beast, harlot, and the last enemy — is read from a chapter that begins with the occupied throne, and the elders’ response is the only fitting one: crowns cast down, and Thou art worthy, O Lord.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The blood-red carnelian of Rev 4:3, describing the appearance of Him that sat upon heaven’s throne.

expand to see more

Sardine stone — Greek sardinos, from Sardis in Lydia; a deep red carnelian.

Rev 4:3 is its one occurrence: the look of Him that sat on the throne.

Paired with the jasper — blood-red justice beside crystal-clear holiness.

The emerald rainbow encircles both: covenant mercy round the throne of the Judge.

The same stone is the sixth foundation of the city wall, there called sardius (Rev 21:20).

Usage

"Like a jasper and a sardine stone: holiness in white light, justice in blood-red fire."

"John saw colour and no countenance — the throne vision refuses the image."

"The rainbow bends clean round: mercy encircles the throne, it does not merely stand beside it."
